elements.subtitle: Key findings from 10 orders across Jan–Mar 2026

elements.text: The dataset covers 10 orders, 179 units, and $15,197 in net revenue across four regions and three categories. Electronics drives the business: it's a minority of units sold but the large majority of revenue, led by a single high-value Laptop line. South is the top region and February was the strongest month.

elements.title: Key takeaway
elements.text: Electronics generates 75% of revenue ($11,346) from just 36 units, while Stationery sells the most units (130) but contributes only 5% of revenue ($700) — the two categories serve very different roles.

South leads with $6,190 (41% of total), more than double East's $1,180. North and West sit in between. One order per region-category combo means these totals are sensitive to individual large orders (e.g. South's Laptop sale).

elements.title: Electronics is the quality + revenue leader
elements.text: Electronics has the highest average customer rating (4.34) and the highest revenue, despite moderate unit volume — a healthy, high-value product line.

Revenue peaked in February ($7,321) then dropped sharply in March ($3,249) — roughly half the January level. With only 10 orders total, this is too little data to call a trend, but it's worth watching whether March's dip continues.
Laptop alone accounts for $7,457.50 — 49% of all revenue from just 2 orders. Desk Chair and Headphones are close behind as the next-strongest performers.

elements.title: Heavier discounts line up with lower ratings
elements.text: The two highest-discount orders (Headphones at 20%, Notebook Pack at 15%) have the lowest or near-lowest customer ratings (3.9 and 3.5). This is a pattern worth testing with more data, not a proven cause — discounting itself doesn't lower satisfaction, but it may correlate with lower-margin, lower-attention SKUs.

items: Investigate the March revenue drop — check if it's seasonal, a sales-cycle gap, or data incompleteness.
Protect Laptop and Desk Chair margins; both sell well with zero discount and high ratings.
Review discounting policy on Headphones and Notebook Pack given the lower ratings at high discount levels.

elements.title: Data limits
elements.text: This dataset has only 10 orders. Regional, monthly, and discount patterns are directional, not statistically robust — treat them as hypotheses to test against a larger sample.
